transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Daniel Lee speaking. How can I help?

Hello, Daniel. It's Rachel Lim. I've finished reviewing the materials and have my notes in front of me. I'd like to keep the call fairly focused, as I'm between consulting meetings. For the account checks, My identification number is G six four seven zero six one nine G. My date of birth is the first of February nineteen seventy.

Thank you, Rachel. I'll keep our conversation concise. Before we get into your notes, how did your gardening project turn out?

The planting is finished, although the patio still needs cleaning. It's been a welcome change from working at a screen. I'm leaving the rest until I have a clear weekend rather than trying to squeeze it around client work.

It sounds as though you've made good progress. I'll leave you to enjoy that without extending this call. We can turn to the notes you have with you.

I've kept the entries in the same order as the materials. The first candidate in my review notes is Summit Global Equity ETF. The next candidate in my notes is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund. I'd like to select the second candidate in my notes for this transaction. My instruction is to buy, not to sell.

I recommend buying Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund.

I'll keep that in mind. Before we work through the rest, could we also settle how to arrange future calls? Unscheduled calls are difficult when I'm working at a client's office.

Certainly. Would you prefer an email to arrange a suitable time, rather than an unscheduled telephone call? We can keep the scheduling message separate from the investment discussion.

An email would be best. Afternoons generally work better, but please wait for my reply rather than assuming I'm free. My consulting diary changes quite often, and I don't always see a missed call until much later.

I'll note that scheduling preference. Returning to our investment discussion, I understand your objective is long-term capital growth through a diversified allocation, rather than concentrating solely on equities. With Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, equity holdings can fall when earnings weaken, and bond holdings can fall when interest rates rise. During market stress, these holdings can decline together, so diversification may offer less protection than expected. Do you understand those risks, including that the fund's equity and bond holdings can decline together?

Yes, I understand. The equity and bond holdings can fall together during market stress, so the diversification may not protect me as much as expected.

You could lose some or all of the capital you invest in this fund. Are you willing to accept the possibility of investment losses with this investment?

Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses with this investment.

Thank you. We can now turn to the remaining details in your notes. I'll leave room for you to finish before I read the instruction back.

I have an existing holding denominated in Japanese yen, but that's separate from the funding and settlement for this purchase. Please use US dollars as the currency for this transaction. The amount I want to commit to this transaction is 150,000. The quantity I want is 1,500 units. For the order type, I was going to say— Let me be precise: please use a limit order with a limit price of 100 American dollars per unit, so I control the execution price.

Please confirm your final instruction: buy 1,500 units of Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, with a transaction amount of 150,000 in US dollars, using a limit order with a limit price of 100 American dollars per unit. Is that your final instruction?

Yes, I confirm that is my final transaction instruction. Please place the order as stated.

Thank you, Rachel. That concludes the instruction discussion. For any routine follow-up, I'll use your scheduling preference rather than interrupting your working day. Is there anything else administrative you wanted to cover?

Nothing else today, thank you. Please keep any scheduling email brief so I can pick it out from the rest of my correspondence. I need to get back to preparing for my meeting now.

Of course. Thank you for calling, Rachel. I'll let you get back to your preparations. Goodbye.

Thank you, Daniel. Goodbye.
